priorFindingsEvidence.FIND-001: REQ-23 (behavioral-spec.md:118-121) now explicitly requires 'Mode A's branch SHALL be REQUIRED to demonstrate -- by a dynamic call-count assertion on the shared function (the same pattern PROP-6 already uses for Mode A's no-publish invariant), not merely a static grep -- that it never calls the shared publish function under any AUTONOMY/branch-selection value that resolves to Mode A, including a deliberately-injected branch-selection bug in the test harness.' PROP-24 (verification-architecture.md:42) mirrors this exactly: 'a DYNAMIC call-count assertion (mock/counter on the shared function, same pattern as PROP-6) proves Mode A's branch makes ZERO calls to it, INCLUDING when the branch-selection logic is deliberately corrupted in a test harness to try to force it (T1)'. The static-grep-only gap is closed.
priorFindingsEvidence.FIND-002: REQ-23 (behavioral-spec.md:112-117) now explicitly defines the shared-unit boundary: 'the pre-publish checks (price/type/eyecatch/visuals) AND the try/except/finally exception-safety (the REQ-21/FIND-004 fix) living INSIDE that shared unit, not re-wrapped or reimplemented per caller ... single source, grep-verifiable: the publish-click statement appears in exactly one file.' PROP-24 (verification-architecture.md:42) operationalizes it as 'the publish-click statement exists in EXACTLY ONE file (grep count == 1: the shared module) ... no duplicated try/except/finally or pre-publish-check logic anywhere else (T1)'. This closes the semantic-only 'no duplicated/reinvented logic' gap with a concrete, mechanically-checkable boundary and oracle.
priorFindingsEvidence.FIND-003: REQ-24 (behavioral-spec.md:124-126) now states 'ON SUCCESS, run.sh SHALL record the SAME fields REQ-22 requires (URL + timestamp + verification result) so V4 (earn) tracking begins exactly as it does for the standalone tool -- a success path SHALL be positively tested, not merely inferred from the absence of a failure test.' PROP-25 (verification-architecture.md:43) requires 'on SUCCESS, records the SAME url+timestamp+result fields REQ-22 requires, positively tested (not inferred from a failure test's absence) (T2)'. The asymmetry (success path untested) is closed.
priorFindingsEvidence.FIND-004: REQ-25 (behavioral-spec.md:132-134) now explicitly closes the installer-template loophole: 'NOT satisfiable by a bundled installer template that pre-sets a fixed value equivalent to a hardcoded default (the config value SHALL be re-readable/mutable at runtime without a code change, and a test SHALL prove changing it changes wake behavior without redeploying code).' PROP-26 (verification-architecture.md:44) requires 'a test proves changing the config value at runtime, no redeploy, changes wake behavior'. The template-equivalent-to-hardcoded-default escape hatch and the missing runtime-mutation test are both closed.
priorFindingsEvidence.FIND-005: REQ-23 (behavioral-spec.md:110-111) now gates on 'the EFFECTIVE mode for the current wake (REQ-25's ratio-derived value, not the raw AUTONOMY variable in isolation)', and REQ-25 (behavioral-spec.md:135-137) requires 'REQ-23's branch-selection logic SHALL consult THIS ratio-derived effective mode, not a raw binary AUTONOMY flag read independently -- a test SHALL prove that setting the ratio to 1-in-N actually produces N-1 Mode-A wakes and 1 Mode-B wake over N consecutive wakes.' PROP-26's T2 test operationalizes exactly this. The dead-configuration risk (ratio stored but never consulted) is closed with an explicit cross-reference and an end-to-end behavioral test.
priorFindingsEvidence.FIND-006: PROP-26 (verification-architecture.md:44, table row) is now marked required: true (✅), consistent with PROP-24/25. The anti-leniency gap (throttle mechanism optional while the mechanics it gates were mandatory) is closed.

evidence.description: REQ-23/24/25 reviewed line-by-line against all 6 iteration-8 findings; all 6 confirmed resolved with concrete, mechanically-checkable language (dynamic call-count assertion, exact shared-unit boundary, positively-tested success path, anti-template-default closure, effective-mode cross-reference, required PROP-26).
PROP-24/25/26 reviewed against REQ-23/24/25; each proof obligation's stated oracle now matches the corresponding requirement's tightened wording word-for-word.

REQ-25's ratio computation has no specified or tested fail-closed behavior for N=0 / missing / malformed ratio config, the sole remaining gap by which the throttle safety property this sprint exists to add could be silently defeated.

freshPassNotes: REQ-23/REQ-25 interaction is now internally coherent for the well-formed case: REQ-23 explicitly gates on 'REQ-25's ratio-derived value, not the raw AUTONOMY variable in isolation', REQ-25 explicitly requires REQ-23 to 'consult THIS ratio-derived effective mode, not a raw binary AUTONOMY flag read independently', and PROP-26's T2 test (ratio=1-in-N => exactly N-1 Mode-A + 1 Mode-B over N wakes) closes the dead-configuration risk for normal N. The one remaining gap found in this fresh pass is the boundary/malformed-input case (N=0, missing config, negative/non-integer N) for the ratio computation itself, which is unspecified and untested (see FIND-001, new this iteration).
summary: All 6 iteration-8 findings (FIND-001 through FIND-006) are RESOLVED with specific, cited, mechanically-checkable spec language and matching proof obligations. One NEW finding (FIND-001, this iteration) remains open: REQ-25/PROP-26 do not specify or test fail-closed behavior for the ratio computation's boundary/malformed-input cases (N=0, missing config, negative/non-integer N), leaving a real gap in the sole mechanism (REQ-25's ratio) that throttles exposure of the irreversible, monetized, unattended publish action this sprint wires in. Overall verdict is FAIL because an open finding exists; this is not a positive-summary PASS.
